questions.question: 1. Which condition is used in the single-threshold method to label a pixel as $1$?

explanations.a: Correct. The single-threshold rule in the experiment labels a pixel as $1$ when $I(x,y) \geq T$.
explanations.b: Incorrect. This condition does not match the labeling rule given for the single-threshold method.
explanations.c: Incorrect. A pixel is not labeled according only to whether its intensity equals zero.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The threshold rule does not require the pixel intensity to equal a value one greater than $T$.

questions.question: 2. Which statement best describes a bi-modal image histogram?

answers.c: It contains only one intensity value
answers.d: It contains an equal number of pixels at every intensity

explanations.a: Incorrect. A bi-modal histogram represents distinct intensity groups rather than an absence of intensity variation.
explanations.b: Correct. A bi-modal histogram has two distinct peaks and can support separation of foreground and background using a single threshold.
explanations.c: Incorrect. A histogram with only one intensity value is not bi-modal.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Equal frequency across all intensities describes a different distribution from the bi-modal case.

questions.question: 3. In region growing, pixels are accumulated into a region based on a test for

explanations.a: Incorrect. File size is not the criterion used to decide whether a neighboring pixel belongs to the growing region.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Coordinates identify pixel locations but do not provide the similarity test used for region inclusion.
explanations.c: Correct. Region growing uses a homogeneity or similarity criterion to decide whether neighboring pixels should be included.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Rotation is not the test used to determine whether pixels are added to the region.

questions.question: 4. OTSU thresholding is described as an automatic threshold-selection method because it

answers.a: selects the threshold by analyzing the image histogram
answers.b: always uses a manually chosen threshold
answers.c: does not use pixel intensity information
answers.d: selects the threshold from the image dimensions

explanations.a: Correct. The experiment describes OTSU as an automatic method that selects a threshold by analyzing the image histogram.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A manually selected threshold is characteristic of manual thresholding rather than the automatic method described here.
explanations.c: Incorrect. OTSU depends on the distribution of image intensities.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Image dimensions are not the basis for the threshold-selection procedure described for OTSU.

questions.question: 5. In region growing, which criterion can be used to decide whether a neighboring pixel is similar to the current region?

answers.a: Whether its file name matches the input image
answers.b: Whether its intensity is within a predefined range of the mean value of the current region
answers.c: Whether its coordinates are identical to the seed coordinates
answers.d: Whether it changes the image dimensions

explanations.a: Incorrect. File naming is unrelated to the similarity test used in region growing.
explanations.b: Correct. One criterion described in the experiment includes a neighboring pixel when its intensity lies within a predefined range of the mean value of the current region.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Neighboring pixels necessarily have locations different from the seed, so coordinate identity is not the stated criterion.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Region growing does not use changes in image dimensions as its similarity criterion.

questions.question: 6. Which statement correctly compares single thresholding and region growing as presented in this experiment?

answers.a: Both methods require a seed pixel as their starting point
answers.b: Single thresholding uses image intensity relative to a threshold, whereas region growing starts from a seed and evaluates neighboring pixels
answers.c: Region growing always uses a bi-modal histogram, whereas single thresholding does not use intensity
answers.d: Both methods operate by changing the spatial resolution of the image

explanations.a: Incorrect. A seed pixel is specifically part of the region-growing procedure, not the single-threshold rule.
explanations.b: Correct. Single thresholding labels pixels according to their intensity relative to a threshold, while region growing begins from a seed and evaluates neighboring pixels using a similarity criterion.
explanations.c: Incorrect. This reverses the roles of histogram information and seed-based region formation described in the experiment.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Neither method is defined as changing the spatial resolution of the image.

questions.question: 7. Suppose an 8-bit image is processed using OTSU thresholding. Over which intensity range is the threshold $T$ selected according to the experiment?

explanations.a: Incorrect. This range excludes intensity values that the experiment includes when considering possible thresholds.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The experiment does not restrict the OTSU search to the lower half of the intensity range.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The experiment does not restrict the OTSU search to the upper half of the intensity range.
explanations.d: Correct. For the 8-bit intensity range used in the experiment, the threshold is selected from $0$ to $255$ by minimizing the within-class variance.

questions.question: 8. If an image contains $k$ objects to be segmented using the region-growing method described in the experiment, how many separate applications of the method are required?

explanations.a: Incorrect. A single application is described as segmenting one object at a time.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The required number of applications depends on the number of objects to be segmented.
explanations.c: Correct. The experiment states that region growing can segment only one object at a time, so $k$ objects require $k$ applications.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The experiment does not require an additional application beyond the number of objects.

questions.question: 9. In OTSU thresholding, the foreground and background are treated as two classes. Which statement describes the objective used to choose $T$?

answers.a: Choose $T$ to maximize the image dimensions
answers.b: Choose $T$ to minimize the weighted within-class variance
answers.c: Choose $T$ so that every pixel has the same intensity
answers.d: Choose $T$ only from the location of the seed pixel

explanations.a: Incorrect. Image dimensions are not the objective used in the OTSU threshold calculation.
explanations.b: Correct. OTSU selects the threshold that minimizes the weighted within-class variance of the foreground and background classes.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The objective is to separate intensity classes, not to make all image pixels equal.
explanations.d: Incorrect. A seed pixel is part of region growing and is not used as the basis for the OTSU threshold.
